resources.string: This version can\'t read a Libre 3
Read glucose from Juggluco on this phone instead.
A Libre 3 is started with an NFC tap. You can read glucose from Juggluco on this phone instead.
The sensor is started by holding the phone to it. NFC has to be on for that.
Sukrara starts the sensor with your LibreView account, like the Libre app does. Then the Libre app can take it back later. Sukrara uploads nothing.
If the Libre app and Sukrara both read the sensor, it can stop working. Swiping it away isn\'t enough: force-stop it (App info › Force stop) or uninstall it before you go on.
Sukrara reads the sensor over Bluetooth. It needs the Nearby devices permission for that.
After the tap, the sensor sends glucose over Bluetooth.
Glucose alerts and \"sensor ends soon\" need notifications. You can allow them later too.
Hold your phone to the sensor
Put the back of the phone on the sensor and keep it there until the phone vibrates.
Keep the phone still on the sensor.
Hold the phone on the sensor a little longer. Trying again is safe.
This isn\'t a FreeStyle Libre 3 or 3 Plus. For another sensor, go back and choose its brand, or read glucose from Juggluco.
Put on a new sensor, then hold the phone to it.
Another app or LibreView account reads it. Stop it there, then try again. Nothing changed on the sensor.
The sensor is started. Keep the phone close.
The sensor is paired. Keep the phone close.
You can close this: Sukrara keeps going in the background.
The sensor is paired. Sukrara connects as soon as Bluetooth is on.
The sensor is paired. Sukrara connects as soon as Nearby devices is allowed.
Keep the phone near the sensor. Sukrara keeps trying in the background.
Glucose readings start when it\'s ready.
Sukrara stops reading the sensor itself and reads glucose from Juggluco on this phone. You can change it in Settings › Sensor.
Sukrara uses your LibreView account only to start sensors with its ID. Your password is sent once to LibreView and never saved.
Signing out keeps the current sensor running. Starting the next one asks you to sign in again.
LibreView has new terms. Accept them in the LibreView or Libre app, then sign in again.
Couldn\'t sign in to LibreView. Check the connection and try again.
Pick the sensor you are wearing. Sukrara reads it on this phone.
Sukrara has never been tested with a real %1$s. It may not connect, and readings may be wrong or missing. Keep your official app or a meter at hand and check every value before you act on it.
Type the 6-character transmitter ID printed on the transmitter or its box. The Dexcom app or receiver must have started the sensor session.
Type the 10-character serial number printed on the sensor\'s box.
Pair the sensor in the Dexcom app first and keep the Dexcom app installed and running. Sukrara reads along with it and sends nothing to the sensor.
Have the sensor cap at hand: when Android asks, type the 6-digit PIN printed on it.
Looking for the sensor. Keep the phone close to it.
The sensor hasn\'t shown up yet. Check the ID you typed and keep the phone close. Sukrara keeps looking.
Type the PIN from the sensor\'s cap in Android\'s pairing dialog.
Connected. Waiting for the Dexcom app: open it so it connects to the sensor.
The sensor has no session running. Start it in the Dexcom app or receiver.
The ID doesn\'t belong to this sensor. Check it and pair again.
The sensor refused the connection. Pair again; if it keeps refusing, the official app may be holding it.
Android\'s Bluetooth pairing didn\'t finish. Pair again and type the PIN from the cap when asked.
Libre 1 and 2 sensors aren\'t read here
This is a FreeStyle Libre 1 or 2. Nothing was sent to it. Sukrara reads the Libre 3 and 3 Plus itself; for this sensor, start it in Juggluco and read glucose from Juggluco.
The phone read another NFC tag, like a card. Hold the back of the phone to the sensor on your arm and try again.
The back of a phone touching the sensor at its NFC spot
Move the phone slowly over the sensor. Take off a thick or metal case. Keep the screen on and unlocked.
Another app may still hold the sensor. Force-stop LibreLink or Juggluco (App info › Force stop) and keep the phone near the sensor.
Keep the phone near the sensor. A sensor paired with another phone can\'t pair here.
